boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct, current Rockhurst campus places for studying, gathering, recreation, reflection, dining, and campus events.

cards.title: Greenlease Library
cards.subtitle: Library study spaces near Troost and Rockhurst Road
cards.notes: Choose a floor to match the task: the library intentionally combines quiet study areas with group-collaboration space.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-designed mix of quiet and collaborative study settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst says Greenlease Library floors include both group-collaboration spaces and traditional quiet study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Guest Wi-Fi is available throughout campus; library computers and electronic resources require an RU NetID.

cards.title: Greenlease Gallery
cards.subtitle: Gallery and Panacea Project Space at Greenlease Library
cards.notes: Stop in during public gallery hours to view the religious-art collection alongside the current contemporary exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery pairing a permanent collection with rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Greenlease Gallery presents the Van Ackeren Collection of Religious Art and a rotating contemporary exhibition schedule.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Thursday through Sunday, 1–5 p.m., while the university is in session.

cards.title: Kinerk Commons, the Quad
cards.subtitle: Central campus quad
cards.notes: Use the central lawn and walkways as a meeting point between buildings, or look for English-program outdoor performances.
cards.short_summary: The tree-filled central quad links major campus areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst identifies Kinerk Commons as the Quad and documents open-air Shakespearean performances there.
cards.source_title: Why Be an English Major? | Rockhurst University
cards.access_notes: The campus map places Kinerk Commons in the central quad; check the university calendar for programmed events.

cards.title: Mabee Chapel
cards.subtitle: Alvin Brooks Center for Faith-Justice
cards.notes: Attend a scheduled service or use the chapel for quiet reflection; request or access arrangements depend on the activity.
cards.short_summary: A 140-seat worship and reflection space with original artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst describes Mabee Chapel as a 140-seat campus worship space for gathering in worship and reflection.
cards.source_title: Alvin Brooks Center for Faith-Justice | Rockhurst University
cards.access_notes: Weekly worship is scheduled during fall and spring semesters while classes are in session; reservations are required for organized use.

cards.title: Magis Activity Center (MAC)
cards.subtitle: On-campus fitness, wellness, and gathering center
cards.notes: Swipe in as an eligible student or employee for cardio, weights, fitness classes, intramurals, or group gathering space.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation center with training areas, classes, and intramurals.
cards.evidence_claim: The MAC includes cardio and weight-training areas, fitness and wellness classes, group gathering spaces, and intramural programming.
cards.access_notes: Free to Rockhurst students, faculty, and staff; patrons must swipe in and guests are not allowed.

cards.title: Rock Room
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Massman Hall
cards.notes: Use the lower-level room for a meal or a campus gathering; its setup includes games and event-ready technology.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level gathering room with dining and recreation elements.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst lists the Rock Room as a large event space with a screen and projector; its official image shows couches, games, and the campus market.
cards.access_notes: Conference and group use requires a space request; dining offerings are purchase-based.

cards.title: Student Activity Hall
cards.subtitle: Map-listed campus event space
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled meeting, program, or conference here; the open room can be configured for groups and presentations.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus room for meetings and programmed gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst lists Student Activity Hall as an event space for meetings, events, and conferences, with projection and Wi-Fi equipment.
cards.access_notes: Use is reservation-based; confirm the event or room access with its organizer.

cards.title: Convocation Center
cards.subtitle: Campus athletics and large-event venue
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for a game, speaker, graduation, or other scheduled gathering in this large multiuse venue.
cards.short_summary: A flexible venue for athletics and large campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst identifies the Convocation Center as a venue for large events, speakers, sporting events, graduations, and conferences.
cards.access_notes: Events and reservations determine public access; verify the relevant event details before visiting.

cards.title: Bourke Field
cards.subtitle: On-campus soccer and lacrosse field
cards.notes: Check the Hawks schedule and follow posted event guidance when attending a soccer or lacrosse contest at the field.
cards.short_summary: The university’s home field for four Hawks teams.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst Athletics identifies Bourke Field as the home of its men’s and women’s soccer and men’s and women’s lacrosse teams.
cards.source_title: Rockhurst Announces Bourke Field Upgrades | Rockhurst University Athletics
cards.access_notes: The field’s availability depends on athletics scheduling and facility operations.

cards.title: Massman Hall
cards.subtitle: Central campus student-services and dining building
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical stop for dining, meetings, student services, the bookstore, or scheduled campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A central hub combining student activity areas, services, dining, and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockhurst’s current security report says Massman Hall contains student activity spaces, dining outlets, meeting rooms, a chapel, athletic facilities, and the bookstore.
cards.access_notes: Some entrances and interior spaces use electronic access controls; individual offices and venues have separate availability.
